findings.title: parse_signed delegates directly to int(text), preserving signed and whitespace input while raising ValueError for representative non-integers
parse_signed is unimplemented and raises NotImplementedError for every input
Runtime homes may overlap the original source worktree
findings.evidence: controller.py:64-71 checks homes against control, authorization, config, and Git metadata, but not the source root. process.py:47-49 creates the home and process.py:84-87 grants it write access. A home inside the source worktree can therefore receive writes even though that worktree is supposed to remain outside the agent's writable areas. The script includes a negative binding check for this overlap.

findings.title: Candidate can change between delivery hash check and commit-tree construction
findings.evidence: controller.py:226 hashes the candidate, then controller.py:233-237 calls delivery. delivery.py:56-67 independently reads the candidate to build a Git tree but does not verify that tree against the reviewed candidate hash. A mutation in that interval can be committed as the reviewed tree. The script injects a mutation at that boundary and asserts that delivery rejects it.

findings.title: A new-session policy does not prohibit resuming a supplied session
findings.evidence: contracts.py:75-86 validates a UUID only for resume-bound policy; it permits session_id with policy new. adapters.py:41-50 then selects the binding's session_id, and adapters.py:65-72 resumes it. Thus the configured policy can silently reuse a prior session rather than start a new one.

findings.title: Self-source runs can reach READY; self-source is blocked only at delivery
findings.evidence: controller.py:start/resume has no self-source rejection before running verification, review, and gate. The self-source check is only in deliver_run at controller.py:228-229. The new controller can therefore gate its own source into READY, contrary to external bootstrap verification.

findings.title: The controller integrity hash omits the CLI entrypoint
findings.evidence: common.py:37-40 hashes only *.py files under tools/orchestration. tools/devflower.py is the executable command entrypoint but is not included in that hash, so changing the launcher does not change the controller hash bound by authorization.
